clue.text: Land from which Shelley met a traveller

definitions.text: Land from which Shelley met a traveller

parts.words: Land from which Shelley met a traveller
parts.note: recalls the opening of Shelley's sonnet Ozymandias, where the speaker meets a traveller from an old, ancient country

explanation.surface: A question about the home country of a traveller in a famous Romantic poem.
explanation.walkthrough: Ozymandias begins 'I met a traveller from an antique land'; the missing adjective is the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The poem's own adjective for the ancient country the traveller came from, meaning very old.

clue.text: Thomas remembered it

parts.note: Edward Thomas's best-known poem opens 'Yes. I remember' followed by the name of a Gloucestershire railway halt

explanation.walkthrough: Edward Thomas, the English poet killed in 1917, wrote a poem named after a village station where his train once stopped.
explanation.definitionFit: A small Cotswold village whose station the poet recalled in his famous poem.

clue.text: Teacher who received valued advice from a prisoner

definitions.text: Teacher who received valued advice from a prisoner

parts.words: Teacher who received valued advice from a prisoner
parts.note: St Paul, writing while imprisoned, sent pastoral letters of counsel to a young church leader

explanation.surface: A schoolmaster takes wise counsel from someone behind bars.
explanation.walkthrough: The New Testament epistles to this disciple are traditionally said to have been written by Paul in captivity.
explanation.definitionFit: Paul's young disciple, a leader and instructor of the early church, to whom two epistles are addressed.

clue.text: Dance play

definitions.meaning: a square dance for four couples popular in the nineteenth century
a stage comedy by Noel Coward of that title

explanation.definitionFit: Both a formal square dance of four couples and the title of a Noel Coward stage comedy.

clue.text: Repeated sound of nymph

definitions.meaning: a sound reflected back to the hearer
the mountain nymph of Greek myth who pined away for Narcissus until only her voice remained

explanation.definitionFit: A reverberation, and the Greek mountain nymph reduced to a voice after loving Narcissus.

clue.text: Spanish talk may give friend a support

parts.note: a pal is a friend
a bra is a supporting undergarment

explanation.surface: Advice in Spanish about giving a companion something to lean on.
explanation.definitionFit: The Spanish noun meaning word or speech, used in English for chatter.

clue.text: Dull speaker with bad pain recalls underworld deity

parts.note: a proser is someone who talks or writes tediously

indicators.note: the word pain is in bad shape, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A boring talker in pain is reminded of a goddess of the dead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bad' is the anagram signal; 'with' and 'recalls' only join the pieces to the definition. Proserpina is the Roman name for Persephone.
explanation.definitionFit: The Roman name for Persephone, queen of the dead as Pluto's wife.

clue.text: Gather information from poet knight

parts.note: Edward Lear, the nonsense poet
N is the chess notation for a knight

explanation.surface: Picking up facts from a poet who is also a knight.
explanation.definitionFit: To acquire knowledge, to find something out.

clue.text: The Barbarians will invite overseas players as well as Grant Allen's

definitions.text: The Barbarians will invite overseas players as well as Grant Allen's

parts.words: The Barbarians will invite overseas players as well as Grant Allen's
parts.note: the Barbarians rugby club picks players from abroad as well as home nations; Grant Allen's novel is titled The ... Barbarians

explanation.surface: A rugby invitation side picks foreign players as well as those of a Victorian novelist.
explanation.walkthrough: Grant Allen wrote the 1895 novel The British Barbarians; the Barbarians are a famous invitation rugby team drawing players from the home nations and abroad.
explanation.definitionFit: The nationality of home players the touring side invites, and the adjective in Grant Allen's novel title.

clue.text: Elizabeth Taylor's backer?

definitions.meaning: the English novelist Elizabeth Taylor wrote a 1957 novel of this title
a financial sponsor of a theatre production

explanation.definitionFit: The title of Elizabeth Taylor's novel about a romantic writer, and slang for a theatrical investor.

clue.text: Sorceress in a mail mix-up

indicators.note: a mix-up of the words a mail means their letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A witch caught up in a postal muddle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mix-up' rearranges A MAIL.
explanation.definitionFit: In Keats's poem and classical myth, a serpent-woman enchantress.

clue.text: Exultation from priest poet at gathering

definitions.text: Exultation from priest poet at gathering

parts.words: Exultation from priest poet at gathering
parts.note: Gerard Manley Hopkins, Jesuit priest and poet, wrote a sonnet of joyful cheering in harvest time

explanation.surface: A clergyman versifies his delight at a gathering.
explanation.walkthrough: Hopkins's sonnet is 'Hurrahing in Harvest'; 'gathering' is the harvest, not a meeting of people.
explanation.definitionFit: Joyful cheering, the shouting of exultant cries, as in the Hopkins poem title.

clue.text: Heard ironic commentaries from woodland gods

indicators.note: heard tells us the word for ironic commentaries is spoken, giving a word of like sound

parts.note: satires are works mocking through irony

explanation.surface: Listening to sardonic remarks from forest deities.
explanation.definitionFit: Goat-like followers of Bacchus haunting the forests in Greek myth.

clue.text: Bracken on slope described by Dylan Thomas

parts.note: bracken is a kind of fern
a hill is a slope

explanation.surface: Bracken growing on a hillside, as in a Welsh poet's verse.
explanation.walkthrough: Fern Hill is Dylan Thomas's poem about his childhood holidays on a Welsh farm.
explanation.definitionFit: The Carmarthenshire farm Thomas evoked in his famous poem of youth.

clue.text: Lone, futile sort of story in French paper

indicators.note: sort of tells us lone and futile are to be sorted into a new order

explanation.surface: A lonely, pointless kind of tale in a Paris newspaper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sort of' rearranges LONE FUTILE.
explanation.definitionFit: A serialised fiction or light literary section printed in a French newspaper.

clue.text: Malraux's novel route

parts.note: Andre Malraux wrote La Voie ..., translated The ... Way, a path through Cambodian jungle

explanation.surface: A French writer's new road.
explanation.walkthrough: Malraux's 1930 novel is La Voie royale; 'novel' looks like 'new' but names the book.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective in the English title The Royal Way, meaning kingly.

clue.text: Badly hampering a loyal follower of Henry V

definitions.text: a loyal follower of Henry V

indicators.note: badly signals that hampering is to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Impeding a king's faithful supporter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Badly' rearranges HAMPERING. Sir Thomas Erpingham is the old knight in Shakespeare's Henry V.
explanation.definitionFit: The elderly knight in Shakespeare's play who served the king at Agincourt.

clue.text: King and academician in indigenous story

indicators.note: in places king and academician within the word for indigenous

parts.note: native means indigenous
R is short for rex, king
RA, Royal Academician

explanation.surface: A monarch and a scholar appear in a local tale.
explanation.definitionFit: A told account of events, a tale.

clue.text: Eliza Haywood's hired lover

parts.note: Eliza Haywood's 1726 novella is The ... Lover, its adjective meaning paid for service

explanation.surface: An eighteenth-century writer's paid paramour.
explanation.definitionFit: Working only for money, as in the title of Haywood's novella.

clue.text: Short paragraph on male beast indicates bright spot over the horizon

parts.note: par is a short form of paragraph
he denotes a male
a lion is a beast

explanation.surface: A brief passage about a male animal points to a light in the sky.
explanation.definitionFit: A mock sun, a bright patch appearing beside the sun from ice crystals.

clue.text: He had a nose for success in the theatre

definitions.text: He had a nose for success in the theatre

parts.words: He had a nose for success in the theatre
parts.note: Edmond ... wrote Cyrano de Bergerac, whose hero has a huge nose, a great stage hit

explanation.surface: A theatrical impresario with an instinct for hits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a nose for success' looks idiomatic but refers to Cyrano's famous nose.
explanation.definitionFit: The French dramatist whose big-nosed hero Cyrano triumphed on stage.

clue.text: One of Jilly Cooper's amendments?

parts.note: Jilly Cooper's novel about show-jumpers is titled with this word in the plural; it also means clauses added to a bill

explanation.surface: A query about changes a novelist made to her text.
explanation.walkthrough: Jilly Cooper is a British bestselling novelist; her book Riders is about horse-jumping.
explanation.definitionFit: A horseman, as in Cooper's novel, and also a clause appended to a legislative bill.

clue.text: Pocket edition of Grass work for a period of inactivity?

definitions.text: Pocket edition of Grass work for a period of inactivity?

parts.words: Pocket edition of Grass work for a period of inactivity?
parts.note: Gunter Grass wrote Dog Years; shorten the years to a briefer unit for the sluggish height of summer

explanation.surface: A small paperback by a German author suits an idle spell.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pocket edition' means a shortened version: Grass's novel Dog Years cut down from years to a smaller span.
explanation.definitionFit: The sultry midsummer spell when little gets done, a period of stagnation.

clue.text: Novelist in premier position

definitions.meaning: he twice served as British prime minister

explanation.definitionFit: The Victorian writer of political novels who also became prime minister.

clue.text: Prohibit first doubtful edition by Arthur Ransome

indicators.note: first takes the opening letter of each of doubtful, edition and by

parts.note: the author's initials

explanation.surface: Banning the dubious first printing of a children's author's book.
explanation.walkthrough: Arthur Ransome wrote Swallows and Amazons; his initials give the last two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To bar or exclude someone from something, forbid.

clue.text: "—! our friend is gone" (Tennyson)

parts.note: fill in the exclamation of grief from Tennyson's line

explanation.definitionFit: An archaic cry of sorrow or regret, like alas.

clue.text: Crane lifted her from city thoroughfares

definitions.text: Crane lifted her from city thoroughfares

parts.words: Crane lifted her from city thoroughfares
parts.note: Stephen Crane's novella is titled ...: A Girl of the Streets

explanation.surface: A machine hoists a woman off the town's roads.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crane' looks like a lifting machine but is the American novelist Stephen Crane.
explanation.definitionFit: The heroine of Crane's novella of New York slum life.

clue.text: Darling dog author

parts.note: Nana is the Darling family's dog in Peter Pan, and Nana is also a novel by a French naturalist writer

explanation.walkthrough: 'Darling' is not endearment but the family name in Peter Pan; their dog's name is a novel title.
explanation.definitionFit: The French writer Emile, whose novel Nana shares the Darlings' dog's name.

clue.text: Moor's father-in-law worries baron a bit

indicators.note: worries means baron and a bit are shaken about into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Othello's in-law frets a little about a nobleman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'worries' rearranges BARON A BIT. Brabantio is Desdemona's father in Othello.
explanation.definitionFit: Desdemona's father, who opposes her marriage to Othello.

clue.text: Latin bible in capital and almost mint condition

indicators.note: in shows the letters are found within the word capital

parts.note: mint condition is A1; almost, it loses its final 1 and leaves A

explanation.surface: An old Latin scripture in near-perfect state kept in the capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' pulls ITAL from inside capital.
explanation.definitionFit: The Old Latin version of scripture predating Jerome's Vulgate.

clue.text: Often associated with ranch hand, especially by Henty

definitions.text: Often associated with ranch hand, especially by Henty

parts.words: Often associated with ranch hand, especially by Henty
parts.note: G. A. Henty's adventure story is titled ... and Cow-boy

explanation.surface: Something commonly linked with cowboys in a Victorian adventure writer.
explanation.walkthrough: G. A. Henty was a Victorian writer of boys' adventure stories.
explanation.definitionFit: A dated, now offensive term for a Native American, paired with the cowboy in Henty's title.

clue.text: Opera composer may be near heaven

indicators.note: may be suggests near could be rearranged into another form

parts.note: the sky is the heavens

explanation.surface: A composer of operas might be close to paradise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'may be' rearranges NEAR into AREN, followed by SKY.
explanation.definitionFit: Anton Arensky, Russian composer of the opera Raphael.
